input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
input.rationale: § 16.2 imposes a blanket consent requirement on IBM's assignments with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard on MSL's consent, which is walk-away territory under this rule (the only reasonableness qualifier runs in MSL's favour for MSL Related Company assignments). It therefore fails even the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice). We redlined the first sentence to add the affiliate/successor carve-out for IBM plus a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, leaving MSL's assignments consent-gated. No change-of-control provisions exist anywhere in the document, so MSL has no termination or re-pricing right on an IBM change of control (§ 16.5 addresses only MSL's own sale or merger and requires the successor to assume performance), which is consistent with the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Add IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and a reasonableness standard in § 16.2.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added our customary carve-out allowing IBM to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made consent for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard. As drafted, § 16.2 blocks IBM's internal reorganizations and corporate transactions entirely, which our playbook does not permit; MSL's assignments remain consent-gated.

ops.oldText: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
ops.newText: Except as expressly permitted below, neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. IBM may assign or transfer all or any part of this Agreement, without MSL's consent, to any IBM affiliate or subsidiary or to any successor by way of merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assets or of the business to which this Agreement relates, upon written notice to MSL.
